title: Strict finite open exchange over completed coefficient rings
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $P_n=A/I^n$, and let $U'=U\times_X X'$ with open immersions $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and maps $g:X'\to X$, $g_U:U'\to U$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. On every small pro-etale site use the completed ring $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$, the strict tower category $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ and reduction $K_\bullet$ of the datum. Let $J_j,J_{j'}$ be termwise sheafified open extension [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let $G_g,G_{g_U}$ be total derived levelwise module pullback on strict towers along the projection-induced completed ring maps, as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Then, for every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$b_K:G_g(J_jK_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{j'}G_{g_U}(K_\bullet)\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(X')).$$
Under the finite-coefficient comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], its $n$-th component is the canonical finite exchange of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] for $\Lambda=P_n$, with finite constant-coefficient pullback as in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact],
$$g_n^*j_!K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n.$$
This isomorphism and its inverse arise from simultaneous strict diagram maps, commute with all quotient transitions, and are linear for the $A_{X'}$-actions through $A_{X'}\to(P_n)_{X'}$. The inverse finite component is the $j'_!\dashv j'^*$-adjoint mate of $g_U^*$ applied to the open unit, followed by the canonical inverse pullback-composition identification. No unrelated morphisms in evaluated derived categories are chosen to define $b_K$. No derived completeness, quasi-compactness or constructibility of $K$ is assumed, and no derived inverse limit is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Use cbcStrictExchange_existsUnique and its chosen specification for the first conjunct. This retains the completed-ring, strict-diagram, ordinary-cartesian-mate normalization: steps 1-6 of the geometric construction are encapsulated in the stated strict-open-exchange interface.

The two finite comparison isomorphisms exist by the normalized finite-comparison existence theorem. They are unique: on a K-flat representative the finite model map is invertible by the scalar-extension counit. Cancel it in the two representative equations. Every complex receives a K-flat quasi-isomorphism; naturality and epimorphic cancellation after localization then give equality on every object, and localization extensionality gives equality of the natural transformations.

Reuse cbcTowerKFlat_resolution from the strict-open-exchange module: its objectwise K-flat tower replacement is constructed by functorial independent-coefficient flat resolution and transposition, and its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Extend the strict counit normalization from these objectwise K-flat tower complexes to every tower complex. Both sides are natural transformations with source Q followed by derived functors. Naturality at the augmentation, its invertibility after Q, and cancellation extend the equality. In particular this applies to the ordinary reduction tower, without asserting that its finite quotients are K-flat over the completed ring.

The ordinary finite scalar compatibility theorem identifies the inverse exchange at every finite coefficient module. Apply it to each cochain degree of the finite reduction. Naturality of cbcUnderivedInverseExchange at the identity-on-sections level coordinate gives the corresponding chain-map equation for cbcSourceLevel and cbcTargetLevel. This is an equality before localization, including the completed scalar actions.

On a K-flat representative P, compare inverse exchanges. Naturality of the strict exchange at cbcReductionModelMap and the extended strict normalization give the strict model square. Evaluate it at n, then use naturality of the evaluation derived-factor comparison and apply Q to the chain-map equation of the preceding step. The defining source and target finite representative normalizations convert its endpoints into the two chosen finite comparisons. Naturality of the derived finite inverse and the exact-functor derived-factor equation identify the remaining finite model square. Cancel the invertible finite source model map to obtain the inverse exchange square on QP.

Resolve an arbitrary complex by a K-flat complex and use naturality and epimorphic cancellation to extend the inverse square to it. Localization extensionality identifies the natural transformations on the whole derived category. Precompose the desired forward square with the evaluated strict inverse and use the two inverse identities to deduce the stated HEq. All ordinary maps were strict natural transformations before localization, so no inverse limit, completeness, constructibility or quasi-compactness assumption occurs.
